hook_text: Every rock you have ever touched has been something else before. Here's the cycle that never stops.
clip_script: Rocks seem like they last forever. They don't. Melted rock cools into igneous rock: slowly underground, it makes granite with big crystals, like Paarl Rock; quickly on the surface, it makes dark basalt, like the Drakensberg cliffs. Wind, water and ice grind rock into sand and mud. Rivers carry it to the sea and drop it in layers, which get pressed and glued into sedimentary rock, like the sandstone on top of Table Mountain, laid down over 400 million years ago. Bury it deep, heat it and squeeze it, and it changes into metamorphic rock: limestone into marble, shale into slate. Push it deeper, and it melts into magma, and the whole cycle starts again. The Sun drives it from above, and the Earth's heat from below.
visual_style: A looping animated rock cycle diagram; time-lapse of Table Mountain; close-ups of granite crystals, sandstone layers and banded gneiss.
pacing: A myth-busting open, three quick rock families, a sweeping loop back to magma, a calm close on the two energy sources.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and identify a rock near your home.
